Dear Garden Members,

Spring has officially arrived at Maple Street Community Garden, and we are thrilled to share the latest news!

First, a big thank you to everyone who joined us for last month's cleanup day. With over forty volunteers, we cleared the beds, repaired the fence, and spread twelve cubic yards of fresh compost. The garden has never looked better.

Planting season is now underway. Plots are available for the cool weather crops, including lettuce, peas, spinach, and radishes. Tomatoes and peppers can go in after the last frost, which we expect in mid-May. If you are new to gardening, our experienced members are happy to offer advice.

Upcoming events include a seed swap on April 20th and a composting workshop on May 4th. Both are free and open to the whole neighborhood, so bring your friends and family.

Finally, we are still looking for volunteers to help with watering during the summer months. If you can spare an hour or two each week, please sign up on the board by the shed.

Happy growing!

The Maple Street Garden Committee
